description_full: Brookfield Business Corporation is a private equity firm specializing in growth capital, divestitures, and acquisitions. The firm typically invests in business services, infrastructure services, construction, energy, and industrials sector. The firm prefers to invest globally. It prefers to take majority controlling stake in companies. The firm seeks returns of at least 15%-20% on its investments. The firm was founded in 2016 and is based in Hamilton, Bermuda.

financial_summary: Brookfield Business Corporation is a mid-cap industrials business with a $6.1B market cap on $27.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -22% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 8.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 10.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 1.2% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -16.0% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 72.9% on average.

own: Insiders own a modest 2.6%, and institutions hold 91%.
It returns 4.5% a year to shareholders (3.7% in buybacks and 0.8% in dividends).
